This application is filed under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short, BNSS), seeking pre-arrest bail.

2. The applicant is the sole accused in Crime No.1505/2025 of Koothattukulam Police Station,
Ernakulam District.

The offences alleged are punishable under Sections 366A, 376 and 376(2) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, and Sections 4(2) r/w 3(a), 8 r/w 7, 6 r/w 5(l) and 10 r/w 9(l) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

sentences.text:
3. The prosecution case, in short, is that the applicant developed an intimate relationship with the survivor girl aged 13 years while she was studying in 9 th Standard, with the deliberate intention to have sexual relationship with her, on several occasions from 5/12/2019 till 30/3/2022, he took the victim to his house situated in Kizhakkombu Kara of Koothattukulam Village, committed sexual assault including penetrative sexual assaults and even thereafter when the victim left India for her higher studies, the applicant followed her through electronic media, threatened her, also uploaded the pictures in Instagram and other social media, thus sexually harassed the 2026:KER:19509 victim and thereby committed the above offences.
4.
I have heard Sri.S.Rajeev, the learned counsel for the applicant and Sri.K.A. Noushad, the learned Senior Public Prosecutor.
Perused the case diary.
5. The learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the above crime.
The counsel further submitted that no materials are on record to connect the applicant with the alleged crime; hence, he is entitled to bail.

The learned Public Prosecutor, on the other hand, submitted that the alleged incident occurred as part of the applicant's intentional criminal acts, and if he is released on bail at this stage, it will affect the course of the investigation.
6. The applicant is now aged 25 years, and the victim is aged 21 years.
The victim is at present in New Zealand pursuing her higher studies.
A reading of the FIS would show that the applicant and the victim met while they were in school.
Their relationship turned to romance over a period of time.

In the FIS, it is alleged that the applicant subjected the victim to sexual assault firstly on 05.12.2019,
secondly, on 22.02.2020 and thereafter on a few occasions till March 2022.
In short, the victim alleges that she was subjected to sexual assault by the applicant for the period from December 2019 to March 2022.

Even though the victim 2026:KER:19509 admits that they were in a romantic relationship, at the same time, she says that all these sexual acts were without her consent and Sreekuttan T Jayan vs State Of Kerala on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162414888/

sentences.text: The veracity of the said allegation has to be tested in the backdrop of documents and pen drive produced by the applicant along with the bail application.

7. Admittedly, the victim left for New Zealand at the end of December 2023 for her higher studies,
and she is still there.

The documents produced by the applicant along with the bail application would indicate that even after she reached New Zealand, she continued to contact the applicant and his family members regularly.
Annexure A6 series to A15 are the printouts of some of the photographs figuring the applicant, victim, and their family members.
It would show that even after the last alleged incident in March 2022, they were in intimate relationship.
Annexure A14 is the screenshot of a story posted by the victim in her Instagram account on 12.01.2024 showing the photograph of the applicant, victim, and some of their common friends.
Annexure A16 is the pendrive containing some of the recordings of video calls made by the victim to the applicant while she was in New Zealand.
I viewed it in the open court.

The conversation between the applicant and the victim in the said video call would suggest that just before the victim filed the complaint against the 2026:KER:19509 defacto complainant, they were maintaining a very close and intimate relationship.
In one of the calls, the applicant invited the victim to come on a private video call, and she agreed to the same.
The screenshot captured during the video calls, which has been produced as Annexure A15 series, also would substantiate the same.

In short, the photographs produced as annexures and video calls copied in a pen drive, produced before this Court, would show that the applicant and the victim maintained a very intimate relationship even after her immigration from India to New Zealand.
Annexure A21(a) is the copy of the complaint given by the victim from New Zealand by mail on 09.07.2025 to the Cyber Crime Police Station, Kochi, against the applicant.
Several allegations were levelled against the applicant under several heads in the said complaint.
It is curious to note that in the said detailed complaint, there is absolutely no whisper of any of the sexual assaults alleged in the present crime.
In these circumstances, the allegations of sexual assaults levelled against the applicant in the FI Statement cannot be swallowed without a pinch of salt.
Considering the allegations made against the applicant, his custodial interrogation seems unnecessary.
For these reasons, I find this to be an appropriate case to grant pre- arrest bail to the applicant.

In the result, the application is allowed on the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall be released on bail in the event of his arrest on executing a bond for Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One lakh only) with two solvent sureties for the like sum each to the satisfaction of the arresting officer/investigating officer, as the case may be.
(ii) The applicant shall fully cooperate with the investigation, including subjecting himself to the deemed police custody for discovery, if any, as and when demanded.

(iii) The applicant shall appear before the investigating officer between 10.00 a.m.
and 11.00 a.m. every Saturday until further orders.
He shall also appear before the investigating officer as and when required.
